transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. Smith, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?
I came in because my in-laws aren't just arguing with me. They're using the altar and the parish committee to push me out, to make everyone forget what I've done for this family.
How long have you felt that your in-laws and the parish committee have been working together to push you out?
About two months now—since that fight with my in-laws over the Día de los Muertos altar.

During these past two months, have you also noticed changes in your mood—like feeling unusually high, energetic, or irritable, or on the other hand, very sad, hopeless, or low—that come and go along with these thoughts?
There were days I felt very bright, very sure of myself. But if anyone questioned me about that altar, I’d snap at them—it felt like they were insulting my whole family.
When you felt that 'bright' and unusually confident, how long would that feeling typically last—was it there most of the day, nearly every day, for a week or more, or did it come and go more briefly?
It’s been going on about two months now, since the fight over the Día de los Muertos altar.
During these two months when you felt unusually bright and confident, did you notice needing much less sleep than usual, yet still feeling full of energy?
At first, yes. I was sleeping only a couple of hours and still getting up with energy to make lists. But now I lie awake before dawn worrying, and I never feel rested.
Even on days when you don't feel especially high-energy or low, do you still find yourself believing that your in-laws and the parish committee are working together against you?
Yes. It’s not just when I’m feeling up or down. I know my in-laws were using the altar and the parish committee to push me out, to make people forget everything I’ve done for this family.
Aside from these beliefs about your in-laws and the parish committee, have you ever heard voices or seen things that others couldn't, or noticed your thoughts becoming jumbled or hard to follow?

On several nights, I heard my late mother’s voice telling me where to put the marigolds and candles. And once—I saw her standing by the kitchen doorway. My husband said nobody was there, but I saw her.
How long have you been hearing your mother's voice or seeing her, and has this happened during times when you weren't feeling especially 'bright' or low?

It was only during that time when I was barely sleeping and rushing around, feeling like I had that special duty with the altar. That’s when I heard her voice and saw her. When my mood dropped, I felt sad and guilty, but I wasn’t hearing or seeing her anymore.
Has there been a stretch of at least two weeks when you were not feeling 'bright'/energetic or down/depressed, but you still believed your in-laws and the parish committee were working against you?
Yes. Even when I wasn’t especially up or depressed, I still knew they were using the altar and the parish committee to push me out and make everyone forget what I’d done for the family.
Now that your mood isn't especially high or low, how many weeks or months have you continued to believe your in-laws and the parish committee are working against you?
About two months now, since that fight with my in-laws over the Día de los Muertos altar.
Out of these past two months, roughly how many weeks in total were you in that high-energy phase or the low, depressed phase, compared to weeks when your mood felt more like your usual self?
It’s all been about two months, since the fight over the altar. I can’t really separate it out into exact weeks beyond that.
How many days or weeks did that period of feeling especially bright, confident, and needing little sleep last before your mood shifted into feeling sad and guilty?
I’m not sure how long that lasted before things changed. I didn’t keep track of the days or weeks.
Right at this moment, would you say your mood feels more like your usual self—neither unusually high nor low—and if so, do you still hold these beliefs about your in-laws and the parish committee?
My mood feels more like myself right now, but yes, I still believe they were using the altar and the parish committee to push me out, to make everyone forget what I’ve done for this family.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a mood episode with manic features (elevated, unusually confident mood, decreased need for sleep with preserved energy, irritability) that later shifted into depressive features (sadness, guilt), consistent with a mixed/bipolar-type mood episode. Concurrently, she experienced hallucinations (auditory and visual of her late mother) that were temporally linked to the manic phase and resolved as mood shifted. Critically, the persecutory delusion (in-laws and parish committee conspiring to push her out) has persisted for the full two months, including a period when her mood was euthymic and neither manic nor depressed—satisfying the requirement for psychotic symptoms occurring in the absence of mood symptoms. Because prominent mood symptoms (manic and depressive) were present for a substantial portion of the illness alongside psychotic symptoms, and delusions have persisted beyond the mood episode, this pattern is most consistent with Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type (F25.0) rather than a mood disorder with psychotic features (F30.2, which requires psychosis only during mood episodes) or Schizophrenia (F20.0, which requires mood symptoms to be brief relative to psychotic illness duration).
